title: Introduction to Node.js and Core Concepts
overview: This lecture provides a foundational overview of Node.js, explaining its architectural roots, how JavaScript traditionally operates in web browsers via engines like V8, and how creator Ryan Dahl embedded Chrome's V8 engine in C++ to bring JavaScript to the backend. It includes live terminal REPL demonstrations and highlights the official definition and prerequisites for learning Node.js.

sections.title: Understanding JavaScript & JS Engines
sections.explanation: JavaScript was originally created as a client-side scripting language intended to make web pages interactive inside web browsers. Browsers cannot run JavaScript directly without a dedicated component called a JavaScript Engine. When users run a web browser, an embedded engine interprets and executes JavaScript scripts. Different browser vendors use different engines: Google Chrome uses the V8 engine, Mozilla Firefox uses SpiderMonkey, and Apple Safari uses JavaScriptCore. Google Chrome's V8 engine is currently the most popular and widely adopted JavaScript engine.

sections.title: Creation of Node.js and Core Capabilities
sections.explanation: Developer Ryan Dahl created Node.js by taking Google Chrome's open-source V8 engine and wrapping it inside C++ code. Because C++ can directly interact with the underlying hardware and host operating system, binding V8 with C++ allowed JavaScript to run outside the browser sandbox. This architecture gives JavaScript access to native machine capabilities, such as direct filesystem handling, read/write operations, and memory management, enabling developers to build server-side applications and web servers entirely in JavaScript.

sections.title: Defining Node.js & Practical Demonstration
sections.explanation: Node.js is defined specifically as a JavaScript Runtime Environment—it is neither a programming language, nor a framework, nor a library. While browser developer consoles allow inline JavaScript execution, standard command-line shells (like zsh or bash) fail to recognize raw JavaScript statements natively. By launching the `node` command in the terminal, users start the interactive Node.js REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) environment, which parses and executes JavaScript directly on the operating system.

sections.title: Official Node.js Definition & Prerequisites
sections.explanation: According to the official documentation on nodejs.org, 'Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.' Because Node.js provides the environment to execute standard JavaScript code outside the browser, having a thorough understanding of core JavaScript fundamentals is a mandatory prerequisite before learning Node.js concepts or backend development.

final_takeaways: Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment, not a language, framework, or library.
Created by Ryan Dahl, Node.js combines Google Chrome's V8 engine with C++ to execute JavaScript outside of web browsers.
Through C++ bindings, Node.js grants JavaScript access to host operating system features like filesystems and memory management.
The `node` terminal command launches an interactive REPL shell for running JavaScript scripts locally.
A solid background in core JavaScript programming is essential before learning Node.js.
